JNCC provides summary data for all internationally designated UK protected areas and their features, plus protected area boundary layers.

JNCC holds datasets for all [Special Areas of Conservation (SACs)](/our-work/special-areas-of-conservation/), [Special Protection Areas (SPAs)](/our-work/special-protection-areas/) and [Ramsar Sites](/our-work/convention-on-wetlands/) in the UK terrestrial and marine environment. These datasets are described below. For datasets specific to UK marine protected areas, please visit the [Marine Protected Area Datasets for Download webpage](/our-work/uk-marine-protected-area-datasets-for-download/).

## Contents

- [Special Areas of Conservation](#special-areas-of-conservation)

- [Special Protection Areas](#special-protection-areas)

- [Ramsar Sites](#ramsar-sites)

- [Further information on national designations](#further-information-on-national-designations)

## Special Areas of Conservation

JNCC maintains datasets for all SACs in the UK.

JNCC provides summary data for all UK SACs and their qualifying habitats and species (spreadsheet format – includes SPAs) and a spatial layer of the SAC boundaries (shapefile format – excludes offshore area). 

The [SAC and SPA spreadsheet](https://hub.jncc.gov.uk/assets/a3d9da1e-dedc-4539-a574-84287636c898) and [SAC shapefiles](https://hub.jncc.gov.uk/assets/52b4e00d-798e-4fbe-a6ca-2c5735ddf049) can be downloaded from the Resource Hub.

Please note, the country nature conservation bodies (CNCBs) periodically update SAC boundaries, for example when natural features shift position. These changes are subtle and may not result in an update to JNCC’s datasets. For the latest SAC boundaries, visit the relevant CNCB webpage (see links below).

SACs with "marine components" are SACs which protect a habitat or species associated with the marine environment. Data for these marine sites can be found on the [Marine Protected Area Datasets for Download webpage](/our-work/uk-marine-protected-area-datasets-for-download/).
 [Top](#toc)

## Special Protection Areas

JNCC maintains datasets for all Special Protection Areas (SPAs) in the UK.

JNCC provides summary data for all UK SPAs and their qualifying bird features (spreadsheet format – includes SACs) and a spatial layer of the SPA boundaries (shapefile format).

The [SPA and SAC spreadsheet](https://hub.jncc.gov.uk/assets/a3d9da1e-dedc-4539-a574-84287636c898) and [SPA shapefiles](https://hub.jncc.gov.uk/assets/20dbc9b4-ceac-4bf2-8763-4ae387fa88c4) can be downloaded from the Resource Hub.

Please note, the country nature conservation bodies (CNCBs) periodically review the qualifying bird species of SPAs and update SPA boundaries, for example in light of new population counts or when natural features of the coastline shift position. JNCC’s datasets may not have been updated to reflect these changes. For the latest SPA datasets, visit the relevant CNCB webpage.

SPAs with "marine components" are SPAs which protect a bird species associated with the marine environment. Data for these sites can be found on the [Marine Protected Area Datasets for Download webpage](/our-work/uk-marine-protected-area-datasets-for-download/).
 [Top](#toc)

## Ramsar Sites

JNCC provides summary data for all UK Ramsar Sites and their habitats and species features (spreadsheet format) and a spatial layer of the Ramsar Site boundaries (shapefile format).

The [Ramsar Site spreadsheet](https://hub.jncc.gov.uk/assets/bc9b0905-fb63-4786-8e90-5f7851bb417d) and [Ramsar Site shapefiles](https://hub.jncc.gov.uk/assets/f0e372e3-1580-4bf4-b31a-2b18ab9ca51d) can be downloaded from the Resource Hub.

 [Top](#toc)

## Further information on national designations

JNCC does not hold datasets for country-level protected areas designated in England, Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland through national legislation, such as: Marine Conservation Zones (MCZs) (England, Wales and Northern Ireland) and Nature Conservation Marine Protected Areas (NCMPAs) (Scotland); Sites of Special Scientific Interest (SSSIs) (England, Scotland and Wales) and Areas of Special Scientific Interest (ASSIs) (Northern Ireland); Areas of Outstanding Natural Beauty (AONBs) (England, Wales and Northern Ireland), National Scenic Areas (Scotland) and National Park (England, Scotland and Wales). Country Nature Conservation Bodies (CNCBs) also hold the latest data for inshore Special Areas of Conservation and Special Protection Areas.

Data for national designation types can be downloaded from the following CNCB websites:

CNCB

Natural Resources Wales

[DataMapWales](https://datamap.gov.wales/)

NatureScot

[SiteLink](https://sitelink.nature.scot/home)

 [Top](#toc)

 Our protected areas represent the very best of our natural landscapes, biodiversity and geodiversity, forming the cornerstone of nature conservation by supporting plants, animals and habitats that are rare or unique.  The 1st NI Countryside Survey was based on a series of surveys between 1986 and 1991on the ecology and landscape of NI. It was carried out under contract for Environment Service (DoENI) and was co-funded by the University of Ulster.

These surveys originated as independent studies of Areas of Outstanding Natural Beauty (AONBs). The aim was to provide consistent information on environmental resources as part of the AONB redesignation process. The surveys were subsequently extended to Fermanagh District and the Wider Countryside in order to cover the whole of NI.

 The Rural Data Hub integrates existing NISRA Census 2021 data into a single, accessible interface, tailored for rural analysis. Its key feature is the ability to create bespoke area profiles at lower geographies by selecting data zones and generating interactive charts with rural/urban comparisons, which can be downloaded for ease of interpretation.

## [NIEA Landscape Action Plan 2026-2027](https://www.daera-ni.gov.uk/articles/niea-landscape-action-plan-2026-2027)

 The Landscape Action Plan forms a key component of the Environmental Improvement Plan for Northern Ireland, responding to the Strategic Environmental Outcome of creating “a healthy and accessible environment and landscapes everyone can connect with and enjoy.”
